usage: For each vector: canonicalize(strict_parse(input)) must equal UTF-8 bytes of expected; each error vector must be rejected. Expected values transcribed from RFC 8785, not generated by the reference implementation.

vectors.description: RFC 8785 §3.2.3 key set: members sorted by UTF-16 code units (U+1F600 sorts before U+FB33 because its UTF-16 lead surrogate is 0xD83D). A code-point sort gets this wrong.
vectors.input: {"\u20ac":"Euro Sign","\r":"Carriage Return","\ufb33":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh","1":"One","\ud83d\ude00":"Emoji: Grinning Face","\u0080":"Control","\u00f6":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis"}
vectors.expected: {"\r":"Carriage Return","1":"One","":"Control","ö":"Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis","€":"Euro Sign","😀":"Emoji: Grinning Face","דּ":"Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh"}

vectors.description: RFC 8785 §3.2.2 example (string and literals members): only quote, backslash and C0 controls are escaped; C0 controls without a short form use lowercase \u00xx; '/' and non-ASCII are emitted raw.
Nested objects sorted recursively, insignificant whitespace removed, I-JSON safe integer bounds preserved.
Non-ASCII emitted as raw UTF-8 (Python json.dumps would escape it as \u00e0) and escaped solidus emitted unescaped.
C0 controls: short escapes where defined, otherwise lowercase \u00xx.

error_vectors.description: Floating-point numbers are forbidden in protocol data.
Duplicate member names are rejected (parser-differential defence).
